scenarios.name: Bigger gas holder
scenarios.description: 2000 Nm3 instead of 1000: less flaring, more CHP hours.

timeseries_inputs.name: maize_window
timeseries_inputs.description: Maize is fed 4 hours a day, from 06:00.

timeseries_inputs.name: slurry_window
timeseries_inputs.description: Slurry is pumped 4 hours every OTHER day, so the feed mix -- and the methane share of the gas -- moves over the run.

levels.name: Gas holder
levels.description: Biogas storage. Its methane share is a tracked component: every inflow carries a share and every outflow draws the holder's own blend, so CH4 is conserved exactly.

flows.name: Feed maize
flows.description: The feeder, on its daily window.

flows.name: Feed slurry
flows.description: The slurry pump, on its two-day window.

flows.name: Biogas
flows.description: The digester's product. CONV() is the released rate, piecewise constant between cohort closings and curve steps; FRACTION() is the methane share of what is being released right now, which follows the feed mix over the days.

flows.name: CHP gas
flows.description: Gas to the engine. AVAILABLE("CHP engine") is 0 while the maintenance failure holds the unit, so the engine stops for exactly the downtime. The start/stop band is HYSTERESIS built from two level thresholds writing chp_gate (on above 850 Nm3, off below 300), which is how a model asks for a minimum on-time; min_rate on top makes the machine semi-continuous -- it runs at 200 Nm3/h or not at all. Each restart crosses the rate threshold and is charged 25 EUR, and counted as the flow's Starts.
flows.rate: AVAILABLE("CHP engine") * min(chp_gas_max, LEVEL("Gas holder") - 150) * (1 if chp_gate > 500 else 0)

flows.name: Flare
flows.description: The safety flare: it opens above 950 Nm3 and keeps the holder off its capacity. The level threshold at 950 is what makes the opening instant exact.

flows.name: CHP electricity
flows.description: Accounting: the methane actually burned times 9.97 kWh per Nm3 of CH4 times the electrical efficiency, sold at 0.18 EUR/kWh (a negative price is revenue).

conversions.name: Digester
conversions.description: Feed in, biogas out over the following days: one release curve and one methane share per feedstock. Cohorts close hourly, which is also the grid every curve step lands on.

info.title: Biogas digester, holder and CHP
info.description: Digester, gas holder and CHP. A purely CONTINUOUS model: two feedstocks are fed on a daily recipe into a digester that releases biogas over the following days (a yield curve per substrate), the gas is stored in a holder whose methane share is tracked as a component, a CHP burns it under a minimum load and a maintenance failure, and the holder flares what it cannot keep. Base unit hours, 30 days.
info.author: Naga
info.notes: Gas is in Nm3 and rates in Nm3/h. The digester starts in the steady state for its average feed (initial_feed_rate), so there is no start-up transient to wait out. The CHP's gas rate reads AVAILABLE("CHP engine"), so its failure stops the engine for exactly the downtime; its min_rate makes it semi-continuous (off, or at least 40 Nm3/h); and its rate threshold charges a 25 EUR start cost every time it restarts, counted as the flow's Starts. Total Cost is the feedstock bill plus the start costs, against the electricity revenue on the CHP output.
